title: Nursing Uganda Medical Images Dictionary & Visual Atlas
description: Categorized high-resolution clinical diagrams, human anatomy plates, and disease reference visuals aligned with UNMEB, UHPAB, WHO, and NCLEX curricula.

images.title: Levels of Structural Organization in the Human Body
images.alt: Diagram showing the 9 levels of structural organization from atom and molecule to organelle, cell, tissue, organ, organ system, and human organism
images.summary: Traces the biological hierarchy from subatomic particles and molecules up to specialized cells, tissues, organs, integrated organ systems, and the complete human organism.
images.clinicalPearl: Nursing pathophysiology begins at the cellular and biochemical level | hypoxia disrupts mitochondrial ATP first before organ dysfunction appears.

images.title: Standard Anatomical Position & Directional Terms
images.alt: Anterior and lateral human figures illustrating Superior, Inferior, Medial, Lateral, Proximal, Distal, Anterior, and Posterior directional terms
images.summary: Anterior and lateral clinical reference illustrating standard anatomical position (erect, palms forward) and paired directional terms used in patient assessment and surgical charting.
images.clinicalPearl: Always document Right and Left from the patient's own anatomical perspective, never the examiner's view.

images.title: Anatomical Body Planes & Sections
images.alt: 3D anatomical human figure showing coronal (frontal), transverse (axial), median sagittal, and parasagittal planes
images.summary: Illustrates the cardinal anatomical sectioning planes | Coronal (Frontal), Transverse (Axial/Horizontal), Median Sagittal, and Parasagittal | essential for interpreting CT/MRI scans and surgical approaches.
images.clinicalPearl: Standard brain and chest CT slices are viewed in the transverse (axial) plane; pelvic labour presentations are taught in sagittal section.

images.title: Major Dorsal & Ventral Body Cavities
images.alt: Lateral and anterior views of dorsal (cranial, vertebral) and ventral (thoracic, abdominal, pelvic) human body cavities
images.summary: Side-by-side lateral and anterior views delineating the protective Dorsal Cavity (cranial and vertebral canals) and Ventral Cavity (thoracic, mediastinal, pleural, pericardial, abdominal, and pelvic cavities).
images.clinicalPearl: The diaphragm separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominopelvic cavity; rupture after blunt trauma can herniate abdominal viscera into the chest.

images.title: Homeostasis & Negative Feedback Loops
images.alt: Diagram comparing a general negative feedback loop (Stimulus, Sensor, Control, Effector) with human thermoregulation above 37 degrees Celsius
images.summary: Shows how physiological sensors, central control centers (hypothalamus/CNS), and effectors reverse deviations from normal setpoints such as core body temperature (37°C).
images.clinicalPearl: Fever shifts the hypothalamic setpoint upward; antipyretics lower the setpoint while tepid sponging assists heat dissipation.

images.title: Atoms, Molecules, Compounds & Epithelial Tissues
images.alt: Chemical building blocks (atom, water molecule, compound) paired with primary epithelial tissue types (squamous, cuboidal, columnar, stratified)
images.summary: Connects foundational chemistry (atoms, molecules, compounds) with the four primary epithelial tissue morphologies lining body surfaces, alveoli, renal tubules, and GI mucosa.
images.clinicalPearl: Simple squamous epithelium enables rapid O2/CO2 diffusion in alveoli, whereas stratified squamous protects high-friction skin and oral mucosa.

images.title: Eukaryotic Human Cell Structure & Organelles
images.alt: Cutaway 3D illustration of a human eukaryotic cell labeling plasma membrane, nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, ER, Golgi apparatus, ribosomes, and lysosomes
images.summary: Detailed 3D cutaway of a human cell identifying every major organelle responsible for ATP synthesis, protein translation, vesicular packaging, and enzymatic digestion.
images.clinicalPearl: Human cells use 80S ribosomes while bacteria use 70S ribosomes | allowing macrolides and aminoglycosides to inhibit bacterial protein synthesis selectively.

relatedTopics.label: The Cell: Basic Unit of Life

images.title: The Cell Cycle & Stages of Mitosis (IPMAT)
images.alt: Horizontal progression of Interphase, Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase, and two genetically identical diploid daughter cells
images.summary: Sequential visual guide to somatic cell division showing DNA replication in Interphase followed by chromosome condensation, metaphase alignment, anaphase separation, telophase nuclear reformation, and cytokinesis.
images.clinicalPearl: Vinca alkaloids and taxanes arrest rapidly dividing tumour cells at metaphase by disrupting mitotic spindle microtubules.

images.title: Human Skeletal System | Anterior & Posterior Views
images.alt: Full anterior and posterior views of the human skeleton with axial and appendicular bones and joints labeled
images.summary: Comprehensive anterior and posterior skeletal atlas highlighting cranial bones, vertebral column (cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacrum, coccyx), rib cage, pectoral/pelvic girdles, and upper/lower limb bones.
images.clinicalPearl: After any long-bone fracture or cast application, always assess the 5 Ps: Pain, Pallor, Pulselessness, Paraesthesia, and Paralysis.

images.title: Human Muscular System | Major Superficial & Deep Muscles
images.alt: Anterior and posterior anatomical views of superficial and deep human skeletal muscles
images.summary: Anterior and posterior views of major skeletal muscles including deltoid, pectoralis major, rectus abdominis, quadriceps femoris, trapezius, latissimus dorsi, gluteus maximus, hamstrings, and gastrocnemius.
images.clinicalPearl: Key intramuscular (IM) injection landmarks include the deltoid, vastus lateralis (preferred in infants), and ventrogluteal sites.

images.title: Classification of Bones by Shape
images.alt: Anatomical comparison of long, short, flat, irregular, and sesamoid bones
images.summary: Compares the five morphological bone classes | Long (femur), Short (carpals/tarsals), Flat (sternum/skull), Irregular (vertebrae), and Sesamoid (patella).
images.clinicalPearl: Flat bones (sternum, iliac crest) retain active red bone marrow throughout adulthood and serve as bone marrow aspiration sites.

images.title: Brain Lobes, Brainstem & Multipolar Neuron
images.alt: Human brain lobes, cerebellum, and brainstem paired with a myelinated multipolar neuron
images.summary: Illustrates the major cerebral lobes, cerebellum, and brainstem alongside a myelinated neuron showing dendrites, soma, axon, and synaptic terminals.
images.clinicalPearl: Assess neurological deterioration early using Glasgow Coma Scale (E-V-M) and pupillary light reflex (CN II / III); GCS <= 8 requires airway protection.

relatedTopics.label: Applied Anatomy & Physiology of the Nervous System

images.title: Whole Blood Composition & Formed Elements
images.alt: Centrifuged blood tube showing 55% plasma, <1% buffy coat, and 45% erythrocytes alongside magnified RBCs, WBCs, and platelets
images.summary: Separates whole blood by centrifugation into straw-gold Plasma (55%), the Buffy Coat (<1% leukocytes and platelets), and Hematocrit/Erythrocytes (45%), with detailed cellular morphology.
images.clinicalPearl: Normal adult hemoglobin is 13–17 g/dL (men) and 12–15 g/dL (women); Hb < 7 g/dL in symptomatic patients warrants urgent cross-match.

images.title: Heart Chambers, Valves & Pulmonary/Systemic Flow
images.alt: Coronal cross-section of the human heart showing chambers, tricuspid/mitral/semilunar valves, and oxygenated vs deoxygenated blood flow
images.summary: Detailed coronal cardiac section showing venous return via SVC/IVC into the Right Atrium and Ventricle (blue deoxygenated arrows) and pulmonary venous return into the Left Atrium, Left Ventricle, and Aorta (red oxygenated arrows).
images.clinicalPearl: The Left Ventricle has the thickest myocardium to generate systemic arterial pressure; left-sided failure causes pulmonary edema while right-sided failure causes peripheral edema and raised JVP.

images.title: Lymphatic System, Thymus, Spleen & Lymph Node
images.alt: Whole-body lymphatic vessels, thymus, spleen, bone marrow, capillary fluid recovery, and lymph node structure
images.summary: Comprehensive lymphatic overview depicting primary lymphoid organs (red bone marrow, thymus), secondary organs (spleen, tonsils, lymph nodes), and interstitial capillary fluid drainage.
images.clinicalPearl: Avoid blood pressure cuffs, venipuncture, or injections on an arm after axillary lymph node dissection to prevent lymphedema.

images.title: Respiratory System, Airway & Alveolar Gas Exchange
images.alt: Upper respiratory airway, trachea, bronchi, and lungs with magnified alveolar O2 and CO2 capillary exchange
images.summary: Connects upper airway anatomy (nasal cavity, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchial tree) with a close-up of alveolar sacs and pulmonary capillaries demonstrating O2 uptake and CO2 elimination.
images.clinicalPearl: Normal adult SpO2 is 95%–100%; SpO2 < 90% signals acute hypoxemia requiring prompt airway clearance and supplemental oxygen.

images.title: Urinary System, Kidney Section & Nephron Unit
images.alt: Kidneys, renal vessels, ureters, and urinary bladder alongside a magnified nephron showing glomerulus, loop of Henle, and collecting duct
images.summary: Shows gross urinary tract anatomy (renal artery/vein, renal cortex and pyramids, ureters, bladder) paired with the functional nephron unit (glomerulus, Bowman's capsule, loop of Henle, peritubular capillaries).
images.clinicalPearl: Minimum safe adult urine output is >= 0.5 mL/kg/hr (>= 30 mL/hr); oliguria below 30 mL/hr is an early bedside warning of dehydration or AKI.

relatedTopics.label: Anatomy and Physiology of the Renal System

images.title: Human Digestive System & Alimentary Canal
images.alt: Labeled anatomical illustration of the human digestive system from oesophagus, liver, gallbladder, stomach rugae, and pancreas to small intestine, colon, appendix, and rectum
images.summary: Labeled regional map contrasting the continuous alimentary canal (mouth to anus) with accessory digestive glands and the bedside abdominal assessment order (Inspect, Auscultate, Percuss, Palpate).
images.clinicalPearl: In acute diarrhea, oral rehydration salts (ORS) restore water and sodium across small-intestinal villi via SGLT1 sodium-glucose co-transport.

images.title: Major Endocrine Glands & Hormone Axes
images.alt: Diagram of human endocrine glands including pineal, hypothalamus, pituitary, thyroid, thymus, pancreas, adrenal glands, ovaries, and testes
images.summary: Maps the central and peripheral endocrine organs governing metabolism, stress response, glucose homeostasis, calcium balance, and reproduction.
images.clinicalPearl: Monitor blood glucose closely in patients on systemic corticosteroids and evaluate neck swelling + dysphagia in thyroid disease.

images.title: Organs of Special Senses | Vision (Eye) & Hearing (Ear)
images.alt: High-resolution anatomical cross-sections of the human eye (cornea, iris, lens, ciliary body, vitreous) and ear (auricle, tympanic membrane, ossicles, cochlea)
images.summary: Pairs sectional ocular anatomy (cornea, anterior/posterior chambers, iris, lens, ciliary body) with complete external, middle, and inner ear anatomy (auricle, tympanic membrane, ossicles, semicircular canals, cochlea).
images.clinicalPearl: To visualize the tympanic membrane safely, pull the pinna DOWN and BACK in children under 3 years and UP and BACK in adults.

images.title: Male Reproductive System | Anterior & Sagittal Views
images.alt: Anterior and mid-sagittal views of male reproductive anatomy including testis, epididymis, ductus deferens, seminal vesicle, prostate, and urethra
images.summary: Coronal and sagittal views detailing the urinary bladder, ureters, prostate gland, seminal vesicles, bulbourethral glands, ductus deferens, epididymis, testis, scrotum, and penile urethra.
images.clinicalPearl: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) compresses the prostatic urethra, causing hesitancy, weak stream, and incomplete bladder emptying.

images.title: Internal & External Female Reproductive Organs
images.alt: Side-by-side external vulval anatomy and coronal cutaway of internal uterus, endometrium, myometrium, fallopian tubes, fimbriae, ovaries, cervix, and vagina
images.summary: Clean dual anatomical view of external genitalia (mons pubis, clitoris, urethral orifice, labia majora/minora, introitus, perineum) and internal organs (uterine fundus, endometrium, myometrium, fallopian tubes, ovaries, cervix, vagina).
images.clinicalPearl: Fertilization normally occurs in the ampulla of the fallopian tube; implantation outside the uterine cavity causes life-threatening ectopic pregnancy.

relatedTopics.label: Internal and External Female Reproductive Organs

images.title: Gravid Uterus & Foetus at Term (Sagittal View)
images.alt: Sagittal pelvic anatomy of term cephalic fetus inside gravid uterus showing placenta, umbilical cord, L4-L5 vertebrae, bladder, pubic symphysis, cervix, and rectum
images.summary: Standardized sagittal obstetrical view linking term foetal attitude and longitudinal cephalic lie to bladder compression, L4-L5 sacrum, and birth canal orientation.
images.clinicalPearl: Always encourage regular voiding or catheterize a distended bladder during labour | a full bladder physically blocks foetal head descent and impairs uterine involution.

images.title: Pre-Eclampsia & Antepartum Haemorrhage (Praevia vs Abruption)
images.alt: Three-column clinical diagram comparing spiral artery vasospasm in pre-eclampsia, placenta praevia over internal os, and abruptio placentae with retroplacental clot
images.summary: Compares hypertensive spiral artery vasospasm (MgSO4 Pritchard regimen) with painless bright-red Placenta Praevia and painful dark-bleeding Abruptio Placentae.
images.clinicalPearl: Strictly NEVER perform a digital vaginal examination in suspected Placenta Praevia; confirm placental site on ultrasound first.

images.title: Plasmodium falciparum Malaria Peripheral Blood Smear
images.alt: Microscopy blood smear showing Plasmodium falciparum ring-form trophozoites inside red blood cells
images.summary: Microscopic blood film showing intra-erythrocytic Plasmodium falciparum ring trophozoites used in confirming malaria diagnosis alongside RDTs.
images.clinicalPearl: Treat uncomplicated malaria with oral Artemether-Lumefantrine (Coartem) and severe malaria urgently with IV Artesunate per Uganda Clinical Guidelines.

images.title: Pulmonary Tuberculosis & Pneumonia Chest Radiograph
images.alt: Chest X-ray radiograph demonstrating pulmonary consolidation and tuberculosis lung pathology
images.summary: Radiographic chest plate demonstrating parenchymal consolidation and upper-zone infiltrates evaluated in pneumonia and pulmonary TB workup.
images.clinicalPearl: Cough > 2 weeks with night sweats and weight loss warrants GeneXpert MTB/RIF sputum testing and airborne IPC precautions.

images.title: Sickle Cell Disease (HbSS) Blood Smear
images.alt: Peripheral blood smear showing crescent-shaped sickled erythrocytes alongside normal biconcave red blood cells
images.summary: Peripheral blood film displaying rigid crescent-shaped drepanocytes responsible for microvascular vaso-occlusion, hemolysis, and acute chest syndrome.
images.clinicalPearl: In vaso-occlusive crisis, prioritize aggressive hydration, warm environment, and prompt multimodal analgesia (avoid cold compresses).

images.title: Skin Layers & Clinical Wound Depth Staging
images.alt: Cross-sectional diagram of Stage 1 to Stage 4 pressure injuries across epidermis, dermis, subcutaneous fat, and muscle/bone
images.summary: Illustrates pressure injury and wound depth progression across Epidermis, Dermis, Subcutaneous Fat, and deep Muscle/Bone (Stages 1–4).
images.clinicalPearl: Reposition bed-bound patients every 2 hours, keep skin clean/dry, and optimize protein intake to prevent pressure ulcers.

relatedTopics.label: Care and Treatment of Pressure Sores

images.title: Clinical Vital Signs & Blood Pressure Measurement
images.alt: Nurse assessing adult patient blood pressure using sphygmomanometer cuff and stethoscope
images.summary: Clinical bedside vital signs assessment plate showing proper brachial cuff placement and auscultation technique.
images.clinicalPearl: Use an appropriately sized cuff at heart level after 5 minutes of quiet rest; record T, P, R, BP, and SpO2 systematically.

images.title: Basic Life Support (CPR) & Emergency Airway Resuscitation
images.alt: Healthcare rescuer performing chest compressions during cardiopulmonary resuscitation training
images.summary: Emergency resuscitation visual demonstrating high-quality chest compression hand placement and BLS team readiness.
structures: Lower Half of Sternum Hand Placement
images.clinicalPearl: Check responsiveness and carotid pulse for no more than 10 seconds before starting high-quality CPR and attaching an AED.

images.title: WHO 11-Step Handwashing Technique (40-60 Seconds)
images.alt: Step-by-step WHO handwashing diagram showing steps 0 through 11 over 40 to 60 seconds
images.summary: Complete 11-step soap-and-water hand hygiene technique aligned with WHO Five Moments for Hand Hygiene to prevent healthcare-associated infections.
images.clinicalPearl: Perform hand hygiene before touching a patient, before clean/aseptic procedures, after body fluid exposure risk, after touching a patient, and after touching patient surroundings.

images.title: Hospital Clinical Waste Segregation | Red, Yellow, Black & Brown Bins
images.alt: Horizontal 4-bin hospital waste segregation chart showing Red Bin for infectious waste, Yellow Safety Box for sharps, Black Bin for non-infectious waste, and Brown Bin for pharmaceutical waste
images.summary: Horizontal Uganda MoH and WHO color-coded hospital waste segregation standard distinguishing infectious/anatomical waste (Red), sharps (Yellow Safety Box), non-infectious waste (Black), and pharmaceutical/chemical waste (Brown).
images.clinicalPearl: Never recap needles; discard used sharps immediately into a puncture-proof yellow safety box sealed at 3/4 full.

images.title: Therapeutic Patient Positions (Supine, Prone & Lateral/Sims)
images.alt: Clinical nursing illustration comparing Supine, Prone, and Lateral Sims recovery positions
images.summary: Visual comparison of core therapeutic bed positions: Supine (dorsal recumbent), Prone (face-down for posterior drainage/ARDS), and Lateral/Sims recovery position.
images.clinicalPearl: Use Lateral or Sims position for unconscious/vomiting patients, enema administration, and rectal examinations to protect the airway.

images.title: Common Pressure Ulcer Sites (Supine & Lateral Positions)
images.alt: Anatomical diagram highlighting high-risk bony prominences for pressure sores including occiput, shoulder, elbow, sacrum, hip, inner knees, and heels
images.summary: Identifies high-risk bony prominences prone to pressure ischemia in immobile patients: occiput/ears, scapulae, elbows, sacrum/coccyx, greater trochanter, medial knees, and heels.
images.clinicalPearl: Turn immobile patients every 2 hours, float heels off the mattress with pillows, and score skin risk daily with the Braden Scale.

images.title: Bristol Stool Chart | Bowel & Elimination Assessment
images.alt: Bristol Stool Chart showing Type 1 through Type 7 stool forms from hard lumps to watery diarrhea
images.summary: Standardized 7-type stool classification guide used at the bedside to evaluate constipation (Types 1-2), normal bowel function (Types 3-4), and diarrhea (Types 5-7).
images.clinicalPearl: Document stool Type, frequency, color (melena, pale, blood-streaked), and hydration status when monitoring gastroenteritis or GI bleeding.

images.title: Nasogastric (NG) Tube Placement & Enteral Feeding
images.alt: Sagittal anatomical routing of a nasogastric tube through the nasal cavity and oesophagus into the stomach alongside syringe gravity feeding
images.summary: Illustrates nasogastric tube insertion past the nasopharynx and oesophagus into the gastric lumen along with gravity syringe enteral feeding.
images.clinicalPearl: Measure NEX (Nose-Ear-Xiphoid) before insertion and confirm gastric placement via pH <= 5.5 aspirate or X-ray before giving any feed or drug.

images.title: Tracheostomy Tube Components & Airway Care
images.alt: Labeled diagram of a cuffed fenestrated tracheostomy tube showing pilot balloon, obturator, inner cannula, flange, outer cannula, and cuff
images.summary: Breaks down key tracheostomy parts required for routine inner-cannula cleaning, sterile suctioning, cuff pressure safety, and emergency recannulation.
images.clinicalPearl: Always keep a spare tracheostomy tube (same size + one size smaller) and obturator at the patient's bedside in case of accidental decannulation.

images.title: Three-Bottle Underwater Seal Chest Drainage System
images.alt: Diagram of a 3-bottle chest tube drainage system with trap collection bottle, underwater seal bottle, and suction manometer bottle
images.summary: Explains pleural drainage mechanics across the collection trap bottle, one-way underwater seal bottle (preventing air reentry), and manometer suction regulator.
images.clinicalPearl: Keep the drainage system strictly BELOW chest level at all times; never clamp a bubbling chest tube routinely as it risks tension pneumothorax.

images.title: Surgical Wound Sutures & Skin Closure Techniques
images.alt: Comparison of surgical wound closure methods including interrupted, continuous, subcuticular, horizontal/vertical mattress, lock-stitch, strips, staples, and tissue glue
images.summary: Visualizes core surgical wound closure patterns: simple interrupted, continuous, subcuticular, horizontal/vertical mattress, locking sutures, adhesive strips, staples, and glue.
images.clinicalPearl: Remove facial sutures early (3-5 days) to minimize scarring, abdominal sutures at 7-10 days, and joint/high-tension sutures at 10-14 days.

images.title: Lower-Limb Skin Traction & Orthopaedic Bandaging
images.alt: Clinical demonstration of lower-limb skin traction with adhesive strapping, elastic bandage wrap, spreader block, and traction cords
images.summary: Demonstrates Buck's lower-limb skin traction application using longitudinal adhesive strapping, figure-of-eight elastic wrapping, spreader block, and free-hanging weights.
images.clinicalPearl: Weights must ALWAYS hang freely off the floor; inspect toes regularly for capillary refill, warmth, sensation, and dorsalis pedis pulse.

images.title: Blood Transfusion | Intravenous Administration Setup
images.alt: Nurse administering blood transfusion via wide-bore peripheral IV cannula from a blood bag on an IV pole
images.summary: Illustrates bedside intravenous blood product transfusion setup using dedicated blood-filter tubing, wide-bore cannula, and continuous clinical monitoring.
images.clinicalPearl: Two clinicians must double-check patient identity, blood group, cross-match tag, and expiry; stay with the patient for the first 15 minutes at slow rate and watch for fever, rigors, or back pain.

images.title: Surgical Wound Drains (Closed Suction vs Open Penrose)
images.alt: Comparison of a closed suction Hemovac evacuator drain and a passive Penrose open surgical drain
images.summary: Compares negative-pressure closed wound drainage (Hemovac evacuator) against open gravity-assisted passive drainage (Penrose drain) used in deep surgical sites.
images.clinicalPearl: Empty closed suction drains when half-full, compress flat before sealing the plug to restore negative pressure, and record exact 24-hour output color and volume.

images.title: Physical Assessment Techniques | Palpation & Percussion
images.alt: Bedside clinical assessment showing two-handed abdominal palpation and indirect percussion using plexor and pleximeter fingers
images.summary: Demonstrates systematic bedside physical examination: light and deep abdominal palpation alongside indirect percussion using the plexor finger striking the pleximeter finger.
images.clinicalPearl: For abdominal assessment, inspect and auscultate BEFORE percussing and palpating so bowel sounds are not altered or tenderness provoked prematurely.

images.title: Lumbar Puncture (Spinal Tap) | L3-L4 Anatomical Site
images.alt: Lateral decubitus positioning and magnified L3-L4 vertebral interspace needle insertion into the subarachnoid space for CSF sampling
images.summary: Shows lateral decubitus (fetal) positioning and magnified lumbar needle entry at L3-L4 below the conus medullaris to collect cerebrospinal fluid safely.
images.clinicalPearl: Because the adult spinal cord ends at L1-L2, inserting at L3-L4 or L4-L5 avoids cord injury; keep patient supine afterward and monitor headache or lower-limb neurology.

images.title: Female Bony Pelvis & Obstetrical Landmarks
images.alt: Anterior anatomical vector diagram of the female bony pelvis showing ilium, ischium, pubis, sacrum, sacral promontory, pelvic brim, ischial spines, and pubic symphysis
images.summary: Illustrates the four bones (two innominate coxal bones, sacrum, coccyx) and four joints of the true obstetrical pelvis, emphasizing gynaecoid landmarks.
images.clinicalPearl: Relaxin softens the pubic symphysis and sacroiliac ligaments in late pregnancy; assess the subpubic arch (>90 deg) for adequate gynaecoid outlet.

images.title: Obstetrical Pelvic Assessment & Conjugates
images.alt: Sagittal and superior pelvic inlet views comparing True, Obstetric, and Diagonal conjugates along with inlet, cavity, and outlet birth diameters
images.summary: Compares True (11.0 cm), Obstetric (10.0 cm), and clinically palpable Diagonal (12.5 cm) conjugates alongside transverse (13.0 cm) and oblique (12.0 cm) pelvic brim diameters.
images.clinicalPearl: Calculate the tightest passage bedside: Obstetric Conjugate = Diagonal Conjugate minus 1.5 to 2.0 cm.

images.title: Female Pelvic Floor Muscles (Levator Ani & Coccygeus)
images.alt: Superior anatomical view of female pelvic floor muscles showing puborectalis, pubococcygeus, iliococcygeus, coccygeus, and urethral, vaginal, and rectal hiatuses
images.summary: Maps the levator ani muscular sling (puborectalis, pubococcygeus, iliococcygeus) and coccygeus supporting pelvic viscera and guiding internal rotation during second-stage labour.
images.clinicalPearl: Teach postnatal Kegel exercises to restore pubococcygeal tone and prevent stress urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse.

images.title: Female External Genitalia & Perineal Anatomy
images.alt: Lithotomy view of female external genitalia showing clitoris, labia, vaginal introitus, perineal body, external anal sphincter, and anus
images.summary: Highlights external vulval landmarks, the central fibromuscular perineal body, and external anal sphincter integrity evaluated during antenatal exams and perineal repair.
images.clinicalPearl: Always perform a systematic rectal-perineal inspection after delivery to detect and repair hidden 3rd- or 4th-degree anal sphincter tears.

images.title: Uterus, Fallopian Tubes, Isthmus & Cervix
images.alt: Coronal section of the uterus, uterine tubes, ovary, fundus, body, isthmus, and cervix
images.summary: Delineates the four uterine regions (fundus, corpus, isthmus forming the lower uterine segment, and cervix), triple-layered myometrium, and adnexal structures.
images.clinicalPearl: Oblique interlacing ('living ligature') myometrial fibres contract strongly post-delivery to compress spiral arteries and stop postpartum bleeding.

images.title: Female Breast & Mammary Gland Anatomy
images.alt: Sagittal anatomical diagram of the lactating female breast showing mammary lobes, lobules, lactiferous ducts, ampulla, nipple, areola, and pectoral muscle
images.summary: Details the 15-20 radial glandular lobes, milk-secreting alveoli, lactiferous ductules, and dual endocrine control by Prolactin and Oxytocin.
images.clinicalPearl: Early skin-to-skin and suckling within 1 hour of birth stimulates maternal Oxytocin, aiding both milk let-down and uterine contraction.

images.title: Menstrual Cycle (Ovarian & Endometrial Phases)
images.alt: 28-day menstrual cycle diagram aligning ovarian follicular/luteal development with endometrial shedding, proliferative growth, ovulation at Day 14, and secretory thickening
images.summary: Correlates ovarian follicle maturation, the Day-14 LH-triggered ovulation, and corpus luteum formation with menstrual, proliferative, and secretory endometrial shifts.
images.clinicalPearl: Estimated Date of Delivery (Naegele's Rule): Add 7 days and 9 months to the first day of the Last Menstrual Period (LMP).

images.title: Fertilization, Cleavage & Blastocyst Implantation
images.alt: Horizontal embryological pathway showing Day 14 ovulation, ampullary fertilization, zygote, 2-cell/4-cell cleavage, morula, blastocyst, and Day 6-7 endometrial implantation
images.summary: Traces ovum release from the ovary, ampullary fertilization, mitotic cleavage to morula (Days 3-4), and blastocyst implantation into decidua (Days 6-7).
images.clinicalPearl: Weeks 3-8 represent organogenesis | avoid teratogenic medications, alcohol, and unprescribed herbal remedies in early first trimester.

images.title: Placenta at Term (Foetal Amnion & Maternal Cotyledons)
images.alt: Side-by-side comparison of smooth shiny foetal placental surface with 3-vessel umbilical cord versus rough lobulated maternal surface showing 15-20 cotyledons
images.summary: Contrasts the smooth amnion-covered foetal surface and central 3-vessel cord (2 arteries, 1 vein) against the rough maternal surface bearing 15-20 cotyledons.
images.clinicalPearl: Always inspect both placental surfaces on a flat tray immediately after delivery | a missing cotyledon or membrane rag causes PPH and puerperal sepsis.

images.title: Foetal Circulation & Three Circulatory Shunts
images.alt: Anatomical vector diagram of foetal circulation labeling umbilical vein, ductus venosus, foramen ovale, ductus arteriosus, descending aorta, and umbilical arteries
images.summary: Illustrates oxygenated placental return via the single umbilical vein through three temporary bypasses | ductus venosus, foramen ovale, and ductus arteriosus.
images.clinicalPearl: First newborn breath drops pulmonary vascular resistance, closing the foramen ovale functionally and converting shunts into adult ligaments.

images.title: Foetal Skull Bones, Sutures & Fontanelles
images.alt: Lateral diagram of the foetal skull labeling frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital bones, anterior fontanelle, posterior fontanelle, coronal and lambdoid sutures, and regions
images.summary: Identifies cranial vault bones, sutures enabling obstetrical moulding, Anterior (Bregma) and Posterior (Lambda) fontanelles, and critical presenting diameters (SOB 9.5 cm).
images.clinicalPearl: Well-flexed vertex presents the smallest AP diameter (suboccipitobregmatic 9.5 cm); full extension gives mentovertical brow presentation (13.5 cm), causing obstruction.

images.title: First Stage of Labour (Cervical Effacement & Dilation)
images.alt: Five sequential coronal panels showing progression from closed uneffaced cervix with mucus plug to 50% effaced, 1 cm fully effaced, 7 cm, and 10 cm full dilation
images.summary: Visualizes progressive cervical shortening (effacement) and opening from 0 cm latent phase through 4-10 cm active labour with intact amniotic membranes.
images.clinicalPearl: Begin plotting the WHO Partograph once active labour starts (>=4 cm cervical dilation); expected dilation in active phase is >=1 cm/hour.

images.title: Second & Third Stages of Labour (Crowning & AMTSL)
images.alt: Side-by-side obstetrical diagrams of second-stage foetal head crowning/extension and third-stage placental separation and uterine contraction
images.summary: Pairs second-stage crowning and cardinal movements with third-stage placental detachment, descent, and Uganda MoH Active Management of Third Stage of Labour (AMTSL).
images.clinicalPearl: Wait for firm uterine contraction before Controlled Cord Traction while guarding the suprapubic fundus upward (Brandt-Andrews manoeuvre) to prevent uterine inversion.

images.title: WHO Modified Partograph & Alert/Action Lines
images.alt: Authentic WHO labour partograph plotting fetal heart rate, liquor/moulding, cervical dilation X along Alert and Action lines, descent O, contractions, oxytocin, pulse, BP, and urine
images.summary: Standardized WHO labour monitoring chart showing cervical dilation ('X') plotted against the Alert line and Action line (+4 hours) alongside foetal heart rate, contractions, and maternal vitals.
images.clinicalPearl: If cervical dilation crosses to the right of the Alert line, reassess bladder, hydration, and cephalopelvic disproportion immediately before reaching the Action line.

images.title: Types of Episiotomy & Perineal Incision Anatomy
images.alt: Perineal diagram illustrating four episiotomy incision lines: Median (1), Mediolateral at 45 degrees (2), Transverse (3), and J-shaped (4) relative to the anus
images.summary: Compares Median, Mediolateral (preferred 45-degree Uganda/WHO standard), Transverse, and J-shaped episiotomies and restricts use to selective clinical indications.
images.clinicalPearl: Routine episiotomy is NOT recommended; perform selective mediolateral episiotomy under Lignocaine 1% only for foetal distress, tight perineum, or operative birth.

images.title: Breastfeeding Positioning & Optimal Latch Technique
images.alt: Comparison of poor nipple-only attachment versus optimal deep areolar latch extending to the junction of the baby's hard and soft palates
images.summary: Illustrates WHO breastfeeding attachment principles contrasting shallow painful nipple sucking against deep asymmetric areolar latch for effective milk transfer.
images.clinicalPearl: Cracked sore nipples indicate poor positioning and shallow latch | correct attachment immediately relieves maternal pain and boosts milk supply.

images.title: Ectopic Pregnancy Implantation Sites
images.alt: Uterus and fallopian tube anatomy showing ectopic implantation sites including ampullar tubal, isthmic tubal, interstitial, infundibular, ovarian, abdominal, and cervical
images.summary: Maps extrauterine implantation locations led by ampullar tubal (~70-80%) and high-rupture-risk isthmic/interstitial sites causing acute haemoperitoneum.
images.clinicalPearl: Any reproductive-age woman with amenorrhoea, lower abdominal pain, and vaginal bleeding or syncope has a ruptured ectopic pregnancy until proven otherwise.

images.title: Salivary Glands & Oral Secretions
images.alt: 3D anatomical view showing parotid, submandibular, and sublingual salivary glands and their oral ducts
images.summary: Illustrates the three paired salivary glands, Stensen and Wharton ducts, salivary amylase starch digestion, and mucosal IgA immunity.
images.clinicalPearl: Routine oral hygiene prevents acute suppurative parotitis in NPO, dehydrated, or ventilated ward patients.

images.title: Anatomy of a Tooth & Human Dentition
images.alt: Coronal section of a molar tooth labeling crown, neck, root, enamel, dentin, gums, pulp, cementum, alveolar bone, and neurovascular supply
images.summary: Details crown/neck/root divisions, enamel, dentine, cementum, neurovascular pulp cavity, and adult permanent (32) vs deciduous (20) dental formulas.
images.clinicalPearl: Inspect oral mucosa and loose dentition prior to solid feeding or endotracheal intubation to prevent aspiration.

images.title: Pharynx Divisions, Oesophagus & Peristalsis
images.alt: Sagittal head and neck anatomy showing nasal cavity, soft palate, uvula, nasopharynx, oropharynx, laryngopharynx, epiglottis, glottis, trachea, and oesophagus
images.summary: Maps the nasopharynx, oropharynx, and laryngopharynx alongside the 25 cm muscular oesophagus, UES/LES sphincters, and epiglottic aspiration protection.
images.clinicalPearl: Feed stroke or drowsy patients upright at 45-90 degrees and hold oral intake immediately if coughing or wet voice suggests aspiration.

images.title: Four Tissue Layers of GI Wall & Peritoneum
images.alt: 3D cutaway diagram of the gastrointestinal wall showing lumen, mucosa, submucosa with Meissner plexus, circular/longitudinal muscularis with Auerbach myenteric plexus, serosa, and mesentery
images.summary: 3D histological cutaway demonstrating the four conserved alimentary wall tunics (Mucosa, Submucosa, Muscularis Externa, Serosa) suspended by vascular mesentery.
images.clinicalPearl: A full-thickness breach through the serosa (e.g., perforated peptic ulcer) leaks gastric acid into the peritoneal cavity causing board-like rigidity.

images.title: Stomach Anatomy, Regions & Gastric Secretions
images.alt: Cutaway textbook illustration of the stomach showing cardia, fundus, body, pyloric antrum, pyloric sphincter, greater/lesser curvatures, three muscularis externa coats, and mucosal rugae
images.summary: Shows stomach regions, triple smooth-muscle coats (longitudinal, circular, oblique), mucosal rugae, and gastric parietal/chief/G-cell secretions.
images.clinicalPearl: Parietal cells secrete both HCl and Intrinsic Factor | loss of Intrinsic Factor leads to Vitamin B12 deficiency (Pernicious anaemia).

images.title: Pancreas Anatomy (Exocrine Ducts & Endocrine Islets)
images.alt: 3D illustration of the retroperitoneal pancreas showing head, body, tail, lobules, main and accessory pancreatic ducts joining common bile duct at duodenal papilla
images.summary: Illustrates the retroperitoneal pancreas head, body, and tail draining pancreatic amylase, lipase, and zymogens alongside endocrine Islets of Langerhans.
images.clinicalPearl: Serum Amylase or Lipase >3x normal with severe epigastric pain radiating to the back indicates acute pancreatitis | keep NPO and resuscitate IV fluids.

images.title: Liver, Gallbladder & Biliary Tract Anatomy
images.alt: 3D anatomical diagram of biliary ducts showing right and left hepatic ducts, common hepatic duct, cystic duct, gallbladder, common bile duct, and ampulla of Vater
images.summary: Traces bile drainage from right/left hepatic ducts into the gallbladder via the cystic duct and down the common bile duct to the ampulla of Vater.
images.clinicalPearl: Gallstones obstructing the cystic or common bile duct trigger RUQ pain (Murphy sign), pale clay-coloured stools, dark urine, and obstructive jaundice.

images.title: Small Intestine Anatomy (Duodenum, Jejunum & Ileum)
images.alt: 3D regional view of the human small intestine highlighting duodenum, jejunum, and ileum relative to the stomach and colon
images.summary: Distinguishes the C-shaped duodenum (iron uptake), coiled jejunum (main nutrient absorption), and terminal ileum (Vitamin B12 and bile-salt recycling).
images.clinicalPearl: Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) activates SGLT1 Na+-glucose co-transport across the small intestine even during acute secretory diarrhoea.

images.title: Intestinal Villi, Microvilli Brush Border & Lacteal
images.alt: Magnified diagram of circular folds, intestinal villi with goblet cells, central green lacteal lymphatic, capillary loop, intestinal crypt, muscularis mucosae, and brush border microvilli
images.summary: Magnifies small-intestinal absorptive architecture from circular plicae to finger-like villi and microvilli brush border enzymes feeding capillaries and lacteals.
images.clinicalPearl: Water-soluble sugars and amino acids enter portal capillaries straight to the liver, while dietary fats enter lacteals to reach venous blood via the thoracic duct.

images.title: Large Intestine Anatomy (Caecum, Colon & Rectum)
images.alt: 3D torso view of large intestine showing caecum, appendix, ascending colon, transverse colon, descending colon, sigmoid colon, rectum, and anus
images.summary: Traces colonic segments from the caecum and appendix through the four colon divisions into the rectum, detailing water recovery and Vitamin K synthesis.
images.clinicalPearl: Colostomy stool consistency follows anatomy: right-sided ascending stomas produce liquid output, whereas descending/sigmoid stomas pass formed stool.

images.title: Digestive Disorders (GERD & Peptic Ulcer Disease)
images.alt: Diagram comparing esophageal, gastric, and duodenal ulcer locations with mucosal/submucosal wall depth cross-section
images.summary: Differentiates gastric vs duodenal peptic ulcer timing and depth alongside GERD reflux management and perforation red flags.
images.clinicalPearl: Suspect GI bleeding or perforation urgently if a PUD patient develops coffee-ground emesis, black tarry melaena stools, or rigid abdominal guarding.

images.title: Oral Medications, Dosage Forms & Safe Administration
images.alt: 3D pills, tablets, and capsules paired with Rights of Medication Administration and enteric-coated safety rules
images.summary: Illustrates oral solid dosage forms, enteric-coated and sustained-release crushing warnings, generic-versus-brand naming, and the 10 Rights of Medication Administration.
images.clinicalPearl: Never crush enteric-coated or sustained-release tablets; monitor closely for overdose toxicity and gastric irritation.

images.title: Pharmacokinetics (ADME) & First-Pass Hepatic Metabolism
images.alt: Hepatic portal vein first-pass liver metabolism diagram alongside Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, and Excretion clinical guide
images.summary: Traces oral drug passage from intestinal absorption through the hepatic portal vein to liver CYP450 first-pass biotransformation, plasma distribution, and renal excretion.
images.clinicalPearl: Always check serum creatinine and eGFR before dosing renally cleared drugs such as gentamicin, vancomycin, digoxin, or tenofovir.

images.title: Pharmacodynamics: Synaptic Receptors & Drug Signalling
images.alt: 3D presynaptic nerve terminal, neurotransmitter vesicles, synaptic cleft, and postsynaptic receptors with agonist versus antagonist action
images.summary: Explains agonist stimulation versus competitive and non-competitive receptor antagonism, EC50 potency, therapeutic index safety margins, and synaptic transmission.
images.clinicalPearl: Narrow therapeutic index drugs such as warfarin, digoxin, lithium, phenytoin, and aminophylline require routine drug level monitoring.

images.title: Intravenous Fluid Therapy, Cannulation & Flow Rates
images.alt: Intravenous infusion bag, drip chamber, sterile tubing, and cannula paired with isotonic, hypotonic, and hypertonic fluid rules
images.summary: Details isotonic (0.9% NaCl, Ringer's Lactate), hypotonic, and hypertonic IV fluid shifts, drip-rate formulas, cannula gauge selection, and VIP phlebitis monitoring.
images.clinicalPearl: Stop the infusion immediately and assess site grade if infiltration, redness, cord-like vein tenderness (phlebitis), or vesicant extravasation occurs.

images.title: Parenteral Routes & Tissue Needle Insertion Angles
images.alt: Cross-section of epidermis, dermis, subcutaneous fat, and muscle showing 90-degree IM, 45-degree SC, 25-degree IV, and 10-to-15-degree ID injection angles
images.summary: Compares exact skin-to-tissue entry angles and anatomical landmarks for intramuscular (90 deg), subcutaneous (45 deg), intravenous (25 deg), and intradermal (10-15 deg) injections.
images.clinicalPearl: Prefer the ventrogluteal site for adult IM injections (avoiding the sciatic nerve) and vastus lateralis in infants under 2 years.

images.title: Autonomic Nervous System (ANS) Receptors & Drug Targets
images.alt: Sympathetic vs parasympathetic dual innervation of pupil, heart, lungs, GI tract, and bladder showing alpha, beta, and muscarinic targets
images.summary: Maps adrenergic (Alpha-1, Beta-1, Beta-2) sympathetic drugs against cholinergic (Muscarinic, Nicotinic) agonists and anticholinergic blockers like atropine.
images.clinicalPearl: Keep Atropine 0.6-1 mg IV immediately available when treating organophosphate poisoning ('SLUDGE' cholinergic crisis) or symptomatic bradycardia.

images.title: RAAS Pathway & Stepwise Antihypertensive Pharmacology
images.alt: Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System cascade showing ACE inhibitors, ARBs, CCBs, and pregnancy-safe methyldopa/hydralazine sites
images.summary: Traces renin, ACE conversion to Angiotensin II, and aldosterone sodium retention alongside ACE inhibitors, ARBs, calcium channel blockers, and obstetric antihypertensives.
images.clinicalPearl: ACE inhibitors and ARBs are teratogenic in pregnancy (use oral methyldopa, nifedipine, or IV hydralazine for pre-eclampsia) and can cause dry cough or angio-oedema.

images.title: Diuretic Sites of Action Along the Renal Nephron
images.alt: 3D nephron diagram showing PCT, Loop of Henle, Distal Convoluted Tubule, and Collecting Duct drug targets for osmotic, loop, thiazide, and potassium-sparing diuretics
images.summary: Locates osmotic (Mannitol), Loop (Furosemide), Thiazide (Hydrochlorothiazide), and K+-sparing (Spironolactone) diuretic action sites and potassium shifts.
images.clinicalPearl: Give diuretics in the morning to avoid nocturia, weigh patients daily on the same scale, and watch hypokalaemia with furosemide vs hyperkalaemia with spironolactone.

images.title: Antibiotic Mechanisms & Bacterial Cell Targets
images.alt: 3D prokaryotic bacterial cell cutaway labeling peptidoglycan cell wall, plasma membrane, 30S/50S ribosomes, nucleoid DNA/RNA, and cytoplasm folate pathway
images.summary: Maps major antibacterial drug classes onto bacterial targets: beta-lactams and vancomycin at the cell wall, aminoglycosides and macrolides at 30S/50S ribosomes, and quinolones/cotrimoxazole at DNA and folate synthesis.
images.clinicalPearl: Collect blood or urine culture & sensitivity (C&S) specimens BEFORE the first antibiotic dose, verify penicillin allergy, and educate on 2RHZE/4RH TB DOTS adherence.

images.title: HIV Life Cycle & Antiretroviral (ART) Drug Targets
images.alt: 3D HIV replication cycle inside CD4 T-lymphocyte highlighting CCR5 entry, reverse transcription, integrase DNA integration, and protease assembly steps
images.summary: Aligns Uganda MoH first-line TLD regimen (Tenofovir + Lamivudine + Dolutegravir) with HIV CD4 binding, reverse transcription, nuclear integration, and protease maturation.
images.clinicalPearl: Reinforce >=95% daily ART adherence and monitor renal eGFR for Tenofovir to achieve viral load suppression (<1,000 copies/mL) and eliminate PMTCT risk.

images.title: Insulin Delivery, Onset Profiles & Antidiabetic Drugs
images.alt: 3D insulin vial, prefilled insulin pen, and U-100 syringe alongside rapid, short, intermediate NPH, and long-acting insulin kinetics
images.summary: Compares rapid, regular soluble, NPH, and glargine insulin peaks, safe 'Clear-before-Cloudy' syringe mixing, metformin contrast precautions, and hypoglycaemia (<3.9 mmol/L) rescue.
images.clinicalPearl: Draw clear Regular insulin BEFORE cloudy NPH insulin into one syringe, rotate abdominal/thigh injection sites, and never omit insulin completely on Type 1 sick days.

images.title: Respiratory Pharmacology: Asthma & Bronchodilators
images.alt: 3D comparison of normal dilated bronchiole versus constricted inflamed asthmatic bronchiole showing smooth muscle constriction and excess mucous
images.summary: Contrasts SABA relievers (Salbutamol) against Inhaled Corticosteroids (Beclomethasone), anticholinergics (Ipratropium), aminophylline toxicity, and acute Status Asthmaticus protocol.
images.clinicalPearl: Always rinse the mouth after inhaled corticosteroids (prevent oral candidiasis), use spacers with MDIs, and avoid non-selective beta-blockers like propranolol.

images.title: Severe Acute Malnutrition: Kwashiorkor vs. Marasmus
images.alt: Side-by-side comparison of children with Kwashiorkor oedematous malnutrition vs Marasmus severe wasting and MUAC threshold
images.summary: Contrasts oedematous Kwashiorkor (moon face, bilateral pitting ankle oedema, distended abdomen, reddish sparse hair) with Marasmus (severe muscle wasting, visible ribs, old-man facies), MUAC <11.5 cm criteria, and F-75 to F-100 therapy.
images.clinicalPearl: Always stabilise SAM children on F-75 first (never rush F-100/high protein during acute phase) and treat occult hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, and infection.

images.title: Measles (Rubeola): Clinical Signs & Vitamin A Care
images.alt: Child clinical progression of Measles showing Conjunctivitis, Coryza, Cough, intraoral Koplik spots, and cephalocaudal rash
images.summary: Illustrates the classic measles 3 Cs prodrome (coryza, conjunctivitis, cough), pathognomonic bluish-white buccal Koplik spots, and downward hairline-to-trunk maculopapular rash.
images.clinicalPearl: Give two doses of oral Vitamin A (200,000 IU if >=12 months) 24 hours apart to prevent measles-related xerophthalmia and corneal blindness.

images.title: Immediate Newborn Care, HBB Resuscitation & KMC
images.alt: Newborn drying, suctioning mouth then nose, APGAR 5-point score, Helping Babies Breathe bag-mask ventilation, and Kangaroo Mother Care
images.summary: Walks through Golden Minute resuscitation (<60 seconds), APGAR scoring at 1 and 5 minutes, C-E clamp bag-valve-mask seal, Vitamin K1 + Tetracycline prophylaxis, and skin-to-skin Kangaroo Mother Care.
images.clinicalPearl: Suction mouth first then nose only if airway is obstructed, stimulate breathing during drying, and initiate bag-mask ventilation within 60 seconds if gasping or apnoeic.

images.title: Uganda UNEPI Immunization Sites & Vaccine Vial Monitor
images.alt: Infant vaccination anatomical sites for Deltoid BCG/Measles and Anterolateral Thigh IM DPT-HepB-Hib/PCV10/IPV beside VVM stages 1-4
images.summary: Identifies pediatric anterolateral thigh (IM) and deltoid (ID/SC) injection landmarks alongside the 4-stage Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) usability key and +2 to +8 deg C cold chain.
images.clinicalPearl: Never use a vaccine vial if the VVM inner square matches or is darker than the outer circle (Stage 3 or Stage 4); keep Epinephrine 1:1000 ready during every immunization clinic.

images.title: Neonatal Jaundice, Kernicterus & Phototherapy Care
images.alt: Clinical comparison of cephalocaudal newborn jaundice and infant receiving overhead phototherapy with protective eye patches
images.summary: Pairs newborn cephalocaudal icterus inspection with safe phototherapy setup featuring opaque protective eye shields, maximal skin exposure, and frequent feeding.
images.clinicalPearl: Any jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours of life is pathologic until proven otherwise and requires urgent sepsis, Rh/ABO, and serum bilirubin workup.

images.title: Paediatric Nephrotic vs. Acute Nephritic Syndrome
images.alt: Child with nephrotic periorbital and ascitic oedema paired with 3D glomerulus, Bowman capsule, afferent and efferent arteriole diagram
images.summary: Connects clinical nephrotic anasarca and periorbital puffiness with glomerular filtration barrier structure to distinguish proteinuric Nephrotic Syndrome from hypertensive haematuric Nephritic Syndrome.
images.clinicalPearl: Weigh nephrotic children daily on the same scale, inspect periorbital oedema before ambulation, and monitor BP closely in post-streptococcal acute nephritic syndrome.

images.title: IMCI Dehydration Assessment & Oral Rehydration (ORS)
images.alt: Clinicians administering oral rehydration therapy alongside UNICEF low-osmolarity ORS 1-litre mixing instructions and Plans A, B, C
images.summary: Demonstrates bedside ORS administration, safe 1-litre sachet reconstitution, and WHO IMCI triage across Plans A, B, and C severe IV Ringer's Lactate resuscitation.
structures: WHO Dehydration Plans A, B & C
images.clinicalPearl: Give small frequent ORS sips by spoon or cup even if a child vomits (wait 10 min then resume slower), add Zinc for 10-14 days, and discard reconstituted ORS after 24 hours.

images.title: Snakebite Envenomation, Insect Stings & Anaphylaxis
images.alt: Human diagram mapping snakebite fang puncture, local swelling, neurotoxic ptosis, shock, and anaphylaxis emergency measures
images.summary: Maps local envenomation signs (fang marks, pain, bleeding, blisters) and systemic neurotoxic/hemotoxic targets while emphasizing safe limb immobilisation and IM Epinephrine.
images.clinicalPearl: NEVER apply a tight arterial tourniquet, cut the bite, or suck venom; immobilise the limb at heart level, run 20WBCT, and give Epinephrine 1:1000 IM immediately for anaphylaxis.

images.title: Rabies Pathogenesis, Hydrophobia & PEP Protocol
images.alt: Bullet-shaped Lyssavirus structure alongside neuronal Negri body inclusion histopathology and WHO PEP protocol
images.summary: Shows bullet-shaped Lyssavirus structural proteins and diagnostic intraneuronal Negri bodies paired with immediate 15-minute wound washing, RIG infiltration, and Essen Day 0/3/7/14 vaccination.
images.clinicalPearl: Rabies is nearly 100% fatal once hydrophobia or neurologic symptoms appear; immediate 15-minute soap-and-water wound flushing plus RIG and vaccine prevents CNS invasion.

images.title: Paediatric Skin Rashes: Varicella vs. Scabies
images.alt: Side-by-side patient photographs showing Varicella polymorphic vesicles on child trunk vs Scabies burrows in interdigital finger webs
images.summary: Differentiates centripetal polymorphic Varicella ('dewdrop on a rose petal' crops) requiring airborne/contact isolation from nocturnal Scabies finger-web burrows treated with Permethrin 5%.
images.clinicalPearl: NEVER administer Aspirin for fever in children with Varicella (risk of fatal Reye syndrome); treat all household contacts at once when managing Scabies.

images.title: Atopic Dermatitis (Eczema) & Contact Skin Allergies
images.alt: 3D forearm flexor plaque eruption with magnified erythematous dermal micro-vesicles inset
images.summary: Depicts acute erythematous micro-vesicles and flexural forearm eczematous plaques guiding lukewarm soak-and-seal barrier repair, trigger avoidance, and topical flare care.
images.clinicalPearl: Apply thick fragrance-free emollient within 3 minutes after a lukewarm bath ('soak and seal') and keep nails trimmed to prevent Staph superinfection.

images.title: Burn TBSA Estimation (Wallace Rule of Nines)
images.alt: Anterior and posterior human body showing Wallace Rule of Nines percentages and Parkland fluid formula
images.summary: Shows adult anterior and posterior total body surface area (TBSA) percentages (Head 9%, Arms 9% each, Trunk 36%, Genitalia 1%, Legs 18% each) alongside Parkland 24h fluid calculation.
images.clinicalPearl: Calculate 24h Parkland fluid volume = 4 mL x kg x %TBSA (give half in the FIRST 8 hours from the time of burn) and monitor urine output closely.

images.title: Cardiovascular Emergencies: Myocardial Infarction & CAD
images.alt: Myocardial infarction coronary thrombus cutaway paired with normal versus atherosclerotic narrowed coronary artery
images.summary: Illustrates acute coronary arterial occlusion causing myocardial ischaemic necrosis alongside progressive lipid plaque narrowing of the coronary lumen.
images.clinicalPearl: Central chest pain >20 min + ST elevation -> Urgent 12-lead ECG, Troponin, O2 (if hypoxic), Aspirin 300 mg, GTN.

images.title: Hypertension, Heart Failure & Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT)
images.alt: Hypertensive left ventricular hypertrophy and vascular atherosclerosis paired with lower-limb deep vein thrombosis valve clot
images.summary: Shows pressure-overload left ventricular hypertrophy progressing to heart failure and atherosclerosis alongside deep calf vein thrombosis at venous valves.
images.clinicalPearl: Unilateral calf swelling/warmth -> Assess DVT risk; elevate limb, initiate anticoagulation, and NEVER massage the calf (PE risk).

images.title: Cerebrovascular Accident (Stroke): Ischaemic vs Haemorrhagic
images.alt: Side-by-side brain comparison of ischaemic thrombotic stroke versus haemorrhagic intracerebral vessel rupture
images.summary: Contrasts cerebral infarction due to arterial thrombosis/embolism (~85%) against intracerebral haemorrhage from a ruptured cerebral artery (~15%).
images.clinicalPearl: Perform BE-FAST assessment -> Obtain urgent non-contrast head CT to exclude haemorrhage BEFORE giving aspirin or thrombolytics.

images.title: CNS Infections: Meningitis, Meningeal Layers & Lumbar Puncture
images.alt: Cranial meningeal layers covering brain paired with lateral lying and sitting lumbar puncture positioning at L3-L4
images.summary: Depicts cranial meninges and subarachnoid CSF space alongside safe lying and sitting lumbar puncture positioning into the L3-L4/L4-L5 interspace.
images.clinicalPearl: Fever + neck stiffness + photophobia (Kernig/Brudzinski+) -> Rule out raised ICP before LP, take cultures, and start IV Ceftriaxone promptly.

relatedTopics.label: Infections of the Central Nervous System (CNS)

images.title: Lower Respiratory Pathology: Pneumonia, Effusion & Pneumothorax
images.alt: Normal vs purulent pneumonia alveoli paired with pleural effusion lung compression and collapsed lung pneumothorax
images.summary: Compares pus-filled consolidated pneumonia alveoli, fluid accumulation in the pleural cavity (effusion), and air-induced lung collapse (pneumothorax).
images.clinicalPearl: High-Fowler positioning, titrate O2 to SpO2 >=94%, and keep underwater-seal chest drainage bottles strictly below chest level without clamping.

images.title: Asthma, Bronchitis & Obstructive Airway Disease
images.alt: Normal dilated bronchiole lumen compared against inflamed asthmatic bronchiole with smooth muscle constriction and excess mucus
images.summary: Contrasts patent healthy bronchiolar lumen against acute bronchospasm, mucosal wall oedema, and thick intraluminal mucus plugging.
images.clinicalPearl: Acute dyspnoea/wheeze -> Administer nebulised Salbutamol + systemic Hydrocortisone; a sudden silent chest signals impending respiratory arrest.

images.title: Renal & Urological Disorders: Calculi, Pyelonephritis & AKI
images.alt: Normal renal cortex, medulla, pelvis, and ureter anatomy paired with obstructing renal calyceal and pelvic kidney stones
images.summary: Pairs internal renal landmarks (cortex, medulla, calyces, pelvis, ureter) with nephrolithiasis stone impaction risking hydronephrosis and acute kidney injury.
images.clinicalPearl: Monitor hourly urine output (<30 mL/h oliguria), assess flank colic and haematuria, strain urine for stones, and check K+ and serum creatinine.

images.title: Urinary Catheterization & Catheter-Associated UTI Prevention
images.alt: Dual-lumen indwelling Foley catheter showing balloon, drainage ports, French size, and four-step CAUTI prevention checklist
images.summary: Identifies Foley catheter anatomy (drainage lumen, 10 mL balloon port, French/mm gauge, bladder opening) paired with aseptic CAUTI prevention steps.
images.clinicalPearl: Confirm urine flow BEFORE inflating balloon with 10 mL sterile water (never normal saline); keep closed drainage bag below bladder level.

images.title: Endocrine Disorders: Goitre, Thyrotoxicosis & Diabetes Mellitus
images.alt: Enlarged goitre thyroid gland lobes paired with Type 1 beta-cell insulin deficiency and Type 2 insulin receptor resistance
images.summary: Illustrates diffuse thyroid hypertrophy (goitre) alongside pancreatic Type 1 absolute insulin loss and Type 2 peripheral cellular insulin resistance.
images.clinicalPearl: DKA emergency -> IV 0.9% NaCl volume resuscitation, regular insulin infusion, and K+ monitoring; assess airway stridor after thyroidectomy.

images.title: Ophthalmic Pathology: Glaucoma, Cataract & Anterior Eye Anatomy
images.alt: Sectional anterior eye anatomy showing lens and Canal of Schlemm paired with real cataract lens opacity and glaucoma drainage block
images.summary: Combines anterior eye cutaway (cornea, lens, iris, ciliary body, Canal of Schlemm), clinical lens cataract opacity, and glaucoma aqueous outflow block.
images.clinicalPearl: Acute angle-closure glaucoma -> severe eye pain, haloes, rock-hard globe (urgent Acetazolamide/Timolol); flush chemical eye burns immediately.

images.title: ENT Disorders: Acute Otitis Media & Exudative Tonsillitis
images.alt: Middle ear ossicles with bulging red otoscopy tympanic membrane paired with tonsillar anatomy and exudative acute tonsillitis
images.summary: Shows middle ear ossicles and Eustachian tube beside otoscopic tympanic bulging, plus normal-versus-inflamed exudative palatine tonsils.
images.clinicalPearl: Otoscopy -> pull pinna up/back (adults) vs down/back (<3 yr); after tonsillectomy monitor frequent swallowing for concealed haemorrhage.

images.title: Haematology: Sickle Cell Disease & Blood Transfusion Safety
images.alt: Crescent sickle red blood cells occluding capillary flow paired with nurse verifying IV blood transfusion
images.summary: Depicts rigid sickle erythrocytes triggering capillary vaso-occlusion compared with normal pliable biconcave RBCs and bedside blood transfusion safety.
images.clinicalPearl: Sickle crisis -> IV hydration, O2, warmth, analgesia; transfusion fever/chills/flank pain -> STOP blood immediately & keep line open with 0.9% NaCl.

images.title: Tropical NTDs: Lymphatic Filariasis & Schistosomiasis
images.alt: Clinical bilateral lower-limb elephantiasis lymphoedema paired with CDC schistosomiasis freshwater snail transmission life cycle
images.summary: Illustrates chronic Wuchereria bancrofti lymphatic obstruction (elephantiasis) alongside snail-borne Schistosoma cercariae transmission to human portal and bladder veins.
images.clinicalPearl: Filariasis -> Albendazole + Ivermectin/DEC & meticulous limb washing; Schistosomiasis -> Praziquantel 40 mg/kg single oral dose.

images.title: Integumentary Pathology: Tissue Perfusion & Gangrene
images.alt: 3D skin vascular plexus layers paired with clinical foot gangrene and dry versus wet gangrene care guide
images.summary: Pairs epidermis, dermis, hypodermis, and cutaneous microvascular plexus with ischaemic diabetic foot gangrene necrosis and wet-versus-dry differentiation.
images.clinicalPearl: Use ANTT aseptic dressing; keep dry gangrene dry pending vascular review, while wet gangrene requires urgent IV antibiotics and surgical debridement.

images.title: Surgical Emergencies: Shock, Haemorrhage & Adult BLS/CPR
images.alt: Proper adult CPR hand placement on lower sternum and underlying heart compression mechanics plus ABCDE haemorrhage shock guide
images.summary: Demonstrates interlocked adult CPR heel placement on the lower sternum (5-6 cm depth, 100-120/min, 30:2) alongside acute haemorrhage shock resuscitation.
images.clinicalPearl: Minimise CPR pauses (<10s) and allow full chest recoil; hypovolaemic shock drops BP late, so act urgently on tachycardia, cool skin, and oliguria.

images.title: Fundamental Vital Signs & Bedside Observations
images.alt: Clinical illustration of nurse taking brachial blood pressure with cuff and stethoscope, pulse oximeter reading 98%, digital thermometer 36.8 C, and bedside vital signs monitor
images.summary: Demonstrates accurate brachial blood pressure auscultation, pulse oximetry, axillary thermometry, and adult resting vital sign reference ranges.
images.clinicalPearl: Cuff bladder width should cover ~40% of arm circumference at heart level; rising RR and falling SpO2 precede shock or arrest.

images.title: The Nursing Process (ADPIE) & Clinical Reasoning
images.alt: Five-step circular ADPIE nursing process workflow paired with stethoscope physical assessment and blood pressure vascular resistance illustration
images.summary: Breaks down the cyclic Assessment, Diagnosis, Planning (SMART), Implementation, and Evaluation nursing framework paired with haemodynamic assessment.
images.clinicalPearl: Diagnose patient responses rather than medical labels, and prioritize Airway-Breathing-Circulation first.

images.title: Pain Assessment (PQRST / 0-10 Scale) & WHO Analgesic Ladder
images.alt: WHO 3-step ascending analgesic ladder alongside 0-10 visual pain faces scale and PQRST pain assessment guide
images.summary: Illustrates WHO oral-first pain escalation from non-opioids to weak and strong opioids paired with PQRST bedside pain assessment and laxative co-prescribing.
images.clinicalPearl: Give chronic analgesia by the clock rather than PRN alone; monitor RR (<12/min) and sedation on Morphine and keep Naloxone ready.

images.title: Palliative Care, Total Pain, SPIKES & Last Office Dignity
images.alt: Four domains of Cicely Saunders Total Pain paired with SPIKES breaking bad news steps and respectful Last Office post-mortem checklist
images.summary: Combines physical, psychological, social, and spiritual 'Total Pain' care with SPIKES compassionate disclosure and dignified Last Office procedures.
images.clinicalPearl: Palliative care affirms life without hastening death; oral/subcutaneous symptom care and empathetic presence preserve dignity.

images.title: Nursing Leadership, Safe Delegation & Conflict Resolution
images.alt: Autocratic, Democratic, and Laissez-Faire nursing leadership styles compared with 5 Rights of Safe Delegation and Tuckman team stages
images.summary: Contrasts ward leadership styles and matches safe clinical task assignment to the Five Rights of Delegation and Tuckman group development stages.
images.clinicalPearl: Accountability cannot be delegated — you remain responsible for verifying delegated vitals and acting on abnormal findings.

images.title: Uganda Health Referral System, HRM & Resource Management
images.alt: Uganda Ministry of Health 7-tier referral pyramid from VHT HC I to National Referral Mulago paired with HRM, FEFO stores, and IDSR surveillance
images.summary: Maps Uganda's seven-tier health facility referral ladder alongside human resource management, FEFO medicine stewardship, budgeting, and IDSR disease notification.
images.clinicalPearl: Apply FEFO (First-Expired, First-Out) in ward stores and notify IDSR epidemic-prone conditions immediately.

images.title: Nursing Ethics, Patient Rights & Medico-Legal Practice
images.alt: Four bioethical pillars Autonomy, Beneficence, Non-Maleficence, and Justice paired with UNMC licensure, NDA medicines, and consent rules
images.summary: Outlines the four foundational bioethical principles alongside UNMC Annual Practising Licence scope, malpractice elements, consent verification, and charting law.
images.clinicalPearl: Only competent adults sign consent (or parent/guardian for minors); draw a single line through charting errors without correction fluid.

images.title: Applied Nursing Research: Process, Sampling & Study Designs
images.alt: Five-chapter nursing research proposal workflow alongside six-tier Evidence-Based Study Design Hierarchy pyramid
images.summary: Structures the five-chapter nursing research proposal (PICO, literature, Kish-Leslie sampling, REC/IRB ethics, APA) with the clinical evidence hierarchy pyramid.
images.clinicalPearl: Always obtain Institutional Research Ethics Committee (REC/IRB) approval and signed consent before collecting patient research data.

images.title: Occupational Health & Safety: Hazard Controls, PPE & Fire
images.alt: NIOSH Hierarchy of Controls inverted pyramid alongside healthcare PPE donning photo, safety goggles, sharps box, and RACE/PASS fire steps
images.summary: Pairs the NIOSH Hierarchy of Controls and five hospital hazard classes with proper PPE donning/doffing sequence, 3/4 sharps safety, and PASS fire response.
images.clinicalPearl: After a needlestick injury wash immediately with soap and water (do NOT squeeze the wound), report, and start HIV PEP within 2h (<72h max).

images.title: Disaster Management Cycle & Mass-Casualty START Triage

images.summary: Visualizes hospital disaster preparedness phases alongside colour-coded START mass-casualty triage using Respirations, Perfusion, and Mental status (RPM).
images.clinicalPearl: Use RPM (<60s check: Respirations, Perfusion, Mental status) to prioritise the greatest good for the greatest number.

images.title: Primary Health Care (PHC), CBHC & Home Visiting

images.summary: Combines Ugandan outreach MUAC screening with aseptic Home Visiting Bag Technique, Primary/Secondary/Tertiary prevention levels, and Alma-Ata PHC elements.
images.clinicalPearl: Place the nursing bag on clean barrier paper above the floor and visit healthy or newborn homes before infectious cases.
